Pool token embeddings into sentence embeddings

Source: R/encode.R
pool.Rd

pool() reduces the token embeddings of each text to one sentence embedding, by mean or CLS pooling. A transformer encoder returns one vector per word piece of a text, whereas a sentence embedding is one vector per text, and the pooling rule is part of the model's definition: Sentence-BERT models average the token vectors over the positions that hold real tokens (mean pooling; Reimers and Gurevych, 2019), while the BGE and mxbai families take the vector of the first, classification token (CLS pooling).

It applies either rule to an array of token embeddings and its attention mask, and by default scales each pooled vector to unit Euclidean (L2) length, the form in which cosine similarity is a dot product. It returns a matrix with one row per text. It is the step encode() runs after the ONNX model, exposed for checking the arithmetic or for pooling token embeddings computed elsewhere.

To embed text, use encode(), which tokenizes, runs the model, and pools with the rule pinned for that model; models(detail = TRUE) lists each model's rule.

Usage

pool(
  token_embeddings,
  attention_mask,
  normalize = TRUE,
  method = c("mean", "cls")
)

Arguments

token_embeddings

Numeric array of token embeddings, shaped texts x tokens x hidden dimensions.

attention_mask

Numeric matrix shaped texts x tokens: 1 for a real token, 0 for padding.

normalize

Scale each pooled vector to unit L2 length (default TRUE).

method

"mean" (default), the average over positions with mask 1, or "cls", the first token.

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per text and one column per hidden dimension, without dimnames.

References

Reimers, N., & Gurevych, I. (2019). Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings using Siamese BERT-networks. Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and the 9th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing (EMNLP-IJCNLP), 3982-3992. doi:10.18653/v1/D19-1410

See also

encode() for embeddings of text; models() for the pooling rule of each pinned model.

Examples

# Two texts, three token positions, two hidden dimensions; the first text
# has two real tokens, the second one.
hidden <- array(1:12, dim = c(2, 3, 2))
mask <- matrix(c(1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
pool(hidden, mask)
#>           [,1]      [,2]
#> [1,] 0.2425356 0.9701425
#> [2,] 0.2425356 0.9701425
pool(hidden, mask, method = "cls")
#>           [,1]      [,2]
#> [1,] 0.1414214 0.9899495
#> [2,] 0.2425356 0.9701425
pool(hidden, mask, normalize = FALSE)
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    2    8
#> [2,]    2    8
